"We set up HubSpot lead scoring, but sales still complains about lead quality."

This happens when lead scoring is treated as a one-time setup rather than an evolving operational tool.

Most teams assign points for basic actions: downloading a guide, opening emails, or visiting a pricing page. But high engagement doesn't always equal high intent. Job seekers, competitors, and casual readers can easily hit a high score without ever having budget or intent to buy.

Effective lead scoring requires a tight feedback loop with sales:
→ Track which high-score leads actually converted into revenue.
→ Deduct points for unfit profiles (like student domains or irrelevant job titles).
→ Review scoring criteria quarterly based on recent deal data.

Lead scoring isn't about giving every action a point. It's about helping sales focus on the right conversations today.
